interpretation.R_weighting_note: R has slightly higher per-instance mean/median IoU than native but slightly lower pooled IoU and slightly higher total FP/FN, so no aggregation-independent superiority claim is supported.
interpretation.SAM_error_shape_note: SAMRefiner has much higher FN mean/median and lower area-ratio mean/median. Its FP median is lower than native while FP mean and total are higher, indicating a skewed or pixel-heavy FP tail rather than uniform FP growth.
interpretation.median_vs_pooled_note: Per-instance mean/median weight instances equally. Pooled IoU and raw TP/FP/FN are pixel-weighted and emphasize large masks/errors.

judgment: The new diagnostic supports substantial adverse same-query geometry change on the 374 native-IoU0.50-matched GT pairs, so fixed S0 ranking cannot be the sole explanation there. It does not support an all-380, AP-equivalent, uniquely causal, or general SAMRefiner claim.

suggested_claim_revision: On the frozen internal DEV187 annotations, among 374 native-IoU0.50-matched GT instances, SAMRefiner reduced same-query mask IoU by median 0.105 and mean 0.113 versus native without rematching; pooled IoU fell from 0.832 to 0.732 with higher aggregate FN and FP. This is conditional geometry evidence, not an all-GT or general failure claim and not a unique explanation of AP loss.

what_results_support: On 374 native-IoU0.50-matched GT pairs, the same SAMRefiner query has materially lower IoU than native/R without rematching.
Both per-instance and pooled summaries show adverse SAMRefiner geometry on the conditional population.
The AP degradation cannot be explained solely by keeping original S0 ranking on these selected pairs.
Typical selected SAMRefiner masks show increased undercoverage/shrinkage, while aggregate FP is driven by a skewed or pixel-heavy tail.
